subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in mode that resets a session immediately after a successful agentic memory flush instead of running compaction, and what consent, timeout, audit, sandbox, and failure boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining behavior changes session retention, silent tool-capable memory execution, provider/model routing, and privacy/security semantics, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
options.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, timeout/cancel behavior, user/audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Fold into reset-memory policy
options.body: Track the remaining behavior under the open reset-memory lifecycle issue so reset-time and compaction-threshold session rotation share one contract.

options.title: Keep compaction as recovery
options.body: Decline automatic reset-after-flush and keep model overrides plus current compaction/exhaustion recovery as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, timeout/cancel behavior, user/audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both the pre-compaction memory flush and /new reset history, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product choice.
